recent_posts.title: From RSS to Atom
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience migrating a personal website from RSS to Atom feeds in 2026, describing it as long-overdue 'impulse coding'. The post covers the key technical differences between RSS and Atom, including Atom's requirement for URI-based entry IDs (using UUID URNs), RFC 3339 timestamps, and explicit content type declarations. A shell command using sed and uuidgen was used to replace old key attributes with UUIDs. To avoid spamming subscribers with re-appearing old posts due to changed IDs, a workaround was implemented to only include new posts in the feed going forward.

recent_posts.title: QuickQWERTY 1.2.3
recent_posts.summary: QuickQWERTY 1.2.3 is a minor bug-fix release for the browser-based touch typing tutor. Two issues are resolved: a broken licence link in the footer introduced when the project migrated from GitHub to Codeberg, and an unnecessary dialog box that appeared when clicking an already-selected keyboard split option (6-7 or 5-6 split) in units 16–20. The project is MIT-licensed and hosted on Codeberg.

recent_posts.title: Apr '26 Notes
recent_posts.summary: Monthly personal notes covering three main topics: a deep dive into the proof of Tutte's theorem on arc-transitive cubic graphs (from Biggs's Algebraic Graph Theory), elementary group theory results on cosets with brief proofs, and updates to Wander Console — a decentralized, self-hosted web discovery tool built with just HTML and JS. The Wander Console now has a network crawler feature and has grown to over 50 consoles recommending 1400+ personal web pages in six weeks. Also includes a brief note on the ctrl+O flush output behavior difference between Debian and macOS.

recent_posts.title: Touch Typing Number Keys
recent_posts.summary: A personal reflection on touch typing number keys, exploring two common methods for assigning fingers to digit keys and a self-devised alternative using the left ring finger for both 1 and 2. The author shares their experience overcoming 20 years of muscle memory to adopt a more comfortable approach, noting that old and new muscle memories can coexist surprisingly well.

recent_posts.title: Multiple URLs in Git Remote
recent_posts.summary: Git remotes can hold multiple URLs, enabling a single push to update several repositories simultaneously. When multiple URLs are added without a pushurl, the first URL is used for fetches while all URLs receive pushes. Setting an explicit pushurl overrides this behavior, restricting pushes to only those specified locations while fetches still come from the first URL. This is useful for mirroring scenarios but should be used carefully, as diverging fetch and push targets can cause confusing state in the local tracking branches.

recent_posts.title: QuickQWERTY 1.2.2
recent_posts.summary: QuickQWERTY 1.2.2 is released, a browser-based touch typing tutor for QWERTY keyboards. This release fixes a bug where the 'Restart' link in the practice pane incorrectly redirected users to Unit 1.1 instead of restarting the current lesson. Additionally, the project's source code has moved from GitHub to Codeberg, marking its third hosting home in 17 years (previously SourceForge from 2008, then GitHub from 2015). The project remains MIT licensed.

recent_posts.title: Wander Console 0.5.0
recent_posts.summary: Wander Console 0.5.0 introduces a built-in console crawler as its headline feature. Wander is a small, decentralized, self-hosted web console that lets website visitors explore pages recommended by independent website owners. The new crawler traverses the Wander network from a base console to discover other reachable consoles. Upgrading requires only replacing the existing index.html with the new bundle. New users can set up their own instance by copying two files to a web server.

recent_posts.title: Wander Console 0.4.0
recent_posts.summary: Wander Console 0.4.0 is released, a decentralized self-hosted web console for exploring community-recommended independent websites. Key changes include wildcard pattern support in ignore lists for filtering unwanted URLs, a new 'via' query parameter that lets website owners track visits originating from Wander Consoles, an improved console picker algorithm that now always includes the starting console in the recommendation pool (removing the need for self-referential links), and relaxed iframe sandbox restrictions to allow links opening in new tabs. The project has grown a community on Codeberg and IRC after a warm reception on Hacker News.

recent_posts.title: HN Skins 0.2.0
recent_posts.summary: HN Skins 0.2.0 is a minor patch release of a browser userscript that adds custom visual themes to Hacker News. This update fixes excessive vertical space below reply links, sorts skin options alphabetically in the selection dialog, and corrects the Terminal skin's navigation bar background color from dark grey to dark green. A few additional minor issues (e.g., wrong monospace font in Cafe and Terminal themes) were found post-release and are already fixed in the GitHub development version, with a formal release planned later.

recent_posts.title: Jan '26 Notes
recent_posts.summary: Monthly notes covering algebraic graph theory topics from the book by Godsil and Royle, including Cayley graphs, vertex-transitive and arc-transitive graphs, bipartite graphs, Tutte's theorem, and Tutte's 8-cage. Also includes a brief JavaScript linear congruential generator implementation and a tip on using `cat -n` vs `nl` for numbering lines in Unix shells, noting that `nl` is POSIX-specified while `cat -n` is not.
